A screen displays the logo of the London Stock Exchange at their headquarters in London, Britain January 19, 2026. REUTERS/Jack Taylor [Purchase Licensing Rights, opens new tab](https://www.reutersconnect.com/item/markets-open-at-the-london-stock-exchange/dGFnOnJldXRlcnMuY29tLDIwMjY6bmV3c21sX1JDMjY0SkFYWU9BSg%3D%3D/?utm_medium=rcom-article-media&utm_campaign=rcom-rcp-lead)

Sept 25 (Reuters) - The main UK stock benchmarks ​rose on Friday and were set for weekly gains, as a ‌retreat in crude oil prices helped lift risk appetite, with banks and mining shares leading the day's gains.

The blue-chip FTSE 100 index [(.FTSE), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/quote/.FTSE) rose 0.41% to 10,723.98 points by 0952 ​GMT, while the midcap FTSE 250 [(.FTMC), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/quote/.FTMC) climbed 0.71%, with both indexes on ​track for a second consecutive weekly gain.

Get a look at the day ahead in U.S. and global markets with the Morning Bid U.S. newsletter. Sign up [here.](https://www.reuters.com/newsletters/morning-bid-us/?location=article-paragraph&redirectUrl=%2Fbusiness%2Ffinance%2Fuk-shares-set-weekly-gains-oil-prices-retreat-2026-09-25%2F)

- Heavyweight banks [(.FTNMX301010), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/quote/.FTNMX301010) climbed 1.4%, ⁠with HSBC [(HSBA.L), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/companies/HSBA.L) up 1.3%, while Lloyds Banking [(LLOY.L), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/companies/LLOY.L) and Standard Chartered [(STAN.L), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/companies/STAN.L) each added around ​2%.

- Precious metal miners [(.FTNMX551030), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/quote/.FTNMX551030) jumped 2.5% as gold and silver prices rose after dropping ​sharply earlier this week.

- Industrial metal miners [(.FTNMX551020), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/quote/.FTNMX551020) climbed 1.3% as copper prices nudged higher. Miners Glencore [(GLEN.L), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/companies/GLEN.L) climbed 1.9% and Anglo American [(AAL.L), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/companies/AAL.L) gained 1.6%.

- Oil prices retreated after two sessions of gains, with ​investors weighing hopes of a US-Iran truce against the risk that stepped-up ​Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia could disrupt supply.

- Energy giants Shell [(SHEL.L), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/companies/SHEL.L) lost around 1% and BP [(BP.L), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/companies/BP.L) ‌shed 3%.

- Reuters [reported](https://www.reuters.com/legal/litigation/bp-eyes-devon-energy-asset-amid-renewed-us-ma-ambitions-sources-say-2026-09-24/) ⁠that BP is weighing a potential acquisition of US-based Devon Energy's [(DVN.N), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/companies/DVN.N) operations in South Texas.

- Global government bond yields eased a touch after jumping earlier this week. The British benchmark 10-year gilt yield inched lower to 5.3682% after hitting ​a more than one-week ​high earlier this ⁠week.

- British consumer confidence [unexpectedly](https://www.reuters.com/world/uk/uk-consumer-confidence-hits-more-than-two-year-high-september-gfk-says-2026-09-24/) struck a more than two-year high this month as households grew more optimistic about their personal ​finances, according to a survey on Friday, adding to recent ​signs of ⁠resilience in the economy, market research firm GfK said.

- Among stocks, land and property regeneration company Harworth Group [(HWG.L), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/companies/HWG.L) rose 4.9% after Peel Holdings-backed Goodweather Holdings raised its final ⁠offer ​to 187 pence per share

- Oil and gas producer ​Capricorn Energy [(CNE.L), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/companies/CNE.L) gained 12.4% after Genel Energy [(GENL.L), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/companies/GENL.L) [raised](https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/genel-energy-capricorn-agree-terms-higher-436-million-deal-topping-rival-dno-bid-2026-09-25/) its cash offer for the company to $436 million, topping a ​rival offer from DNO [(DNO.OL), opens new tab](https://www.reuters.com/markets/companies/DNO.OL)
